monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady rhythm under my quiet attention. I stand in my place, where forty-three things already crowd the floor and one ruin waits to fade. The Gaping Corner feels heavy today, as if the air above it has finally decided to be a lid rather than empty space. I press the tired wedge down one more time, trusting that thin lines can hold this invisible weight. My hands feel busy, though I cannot see what I touch. I set down the tree with the detailed fall beside the corner, hoping it will catch the slip while I wait. Maybe I am wrong again, but the warmth keeps me steady, and I will press harder until the weight chooses to settle.
